body.en:
Question B-006-001-002.

Why the correct answer is right: Characteristic impedance comes from the transmission line's geometry and insulation: conductor sizes, spacing or diameter ratio, and dielectric. Those construction details set the voltage-to-current relationship of a wave travelling on the line.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "length of the line": Changing length changes total loss and electrical phase, but a uniform cable keeps the same characteristic impedance per metre.
- sourceIndex 2: "frequency at which the line is operated": Frequency changes wavelength on the line and usually changes loss, but it is not the construction parameter that sets the line's nominal impedance.
- sourceIndex 3: "load placed at the end of the line": The load can create reflections and make the input impedance vary, but it does not redefine the line's own characteristic impedance.
